name: Diodorus of Sardis
bio: Diodorus of Sardis is one of the epigrammatists whose short poems were gathered in the Greek Anthology. Paton's index of authors dates the poet to 1st century AD. Paton's index lists the poet among the writers of the Wreath of Philippus, the Garland compiled in the first century AD.
This archive carries the 9 epigrams ascribed to the poet in the second volume of W. R. Paton's prose translation (Book VII: 38, 40, 74, 370, 624, 627, 632, 700, 701).

poems.title: Book VII, 38: On Aristophanes
poems.author: Diodorus of Sardis
poems.text: Divine Aristophanes lies dead beneath me. If thou askest which, it is the comic poet who keeps the memory of the old stage alive.

poems.title: Book VII, 40: On the Same
poems.author: Diodorus of Sardis
poems.text: This tombstone says that Aeschylus the great lies here, far from his own Attica, by the white waters of Sicilian Gelas. What spiteful grudge against the good is this, alas, that ever besets the sons of Theseus?

poems.title: Book VII, 74: On the Same
poems.author: Diodorus of Sardis
poems.text: The people of Magnesia raised to Themistocles this monument in a land not his own, when after saving his country from the Medes, he was laid in foreign earth under a foreign stone. Verily Envy so willed, and deeds of valour have less privilege than she.

poems.title: Book VII, 370
poems.author: Diodorus of Sardis
poems.text: Menander of Athens, the son of Diopeithes, the friend of Bacchus and the Muses, rests beneath me, or at least the little dust he shed in the funeral fire. But if thou seekest Menander himself thou shalt find him in the abode of Zeus or in the Islands of the Blest.

poems.title: Book VII, 624
poems.author: Diodorus of Sardis
poems.text: Our on thee, dreaded Ionian Sea, pitiless water, ferrier of men to blackest Hades, thou who hast engulfed so many. Who, with the fate of the unfortunates before his eyes, shall tell all thy crimes, ill-starred sea? Thou hast swallowed in thy surges Aegeus and Labeo, with their short-lived companions and their whole ship.

poems.title: Book VII, 627
poems.author: Diodorus of Sardis
poems.text: Leaving thy bridal-chamber half prepared, thy wedding close at hand, thou hast gone, young man, down the baneful road of Hades; and sorely hast thou afflicted Thynion of Astacus, who most piteously of all lamented for thee, dead in thy prime, weeping for the evil fate of her Hipparchus, seeing thou didst complete but twenty-four years.

poems.title: Book VII, 632
poems.author: Diodorus of Sardis
poems.text: A little child in Diodorus’ house fell from a little ladder, but falling head first broke the vertebra of its neck, to break which is fatal. But when it saw its revered master running up, it at once stretched out its baby arms to him. Earth, never lie heavy on the bones of the little slave child, but be kind to two-year-old Corax.

poems.title: Book VII, 700
poems.author: Diodorus of Sardis
poems.text: Know, thou stone palace of the Night that hides me, and thou, flood of Cocytus, where wailing is loud, it was not my husband, as they say, who, contemplating another marriage, slew me. Why should Rufinus have that evil name for naught? But the fatal Destinies brought me here. Paula of Tarentum is not the only woman who has died before her time.

poems.title: Book VII, 701
poems.author: Diodorus of Sardis
poems.text: His dear city set up this inscription by the beautiful waters of Ascania to the strong man Achaeus. Nicaea wept for him, and his father Diomedes erected to him this tall and glittering stone monument, lamenting; for it had been meeter for his son to pay him these honours when he died himself.

poems.title: Book IX, 60
poems.author: Diodorus of Sardis
poems.text: I, THIs tower on the rock in the sea, am Pharos, bearing the same name as the island and serving asa beacon for the harbour.

poems.title: Book IX, 219
poems.author: Diodorus of Sardis
poems.text: As, in days of old, Neoptolemus, the son of Achilles, sailed to Troy from the goat-pastures of Scyrus, so among the sons of Aeneas doth their leader Nero return to the city of Remus, entering from the sea swift-flowing Tiber, a youth with the first down on his cheeks. The other’s force was in his spear alone; this youth is strong both in battle and in the schools.

poems.title: Book IX, 405
poems.author: Diodorus of Sardis
poems.text: May holy Adrasteia preserve thee, and Nemesis, the maiden who treadeth in our track, she who has cheated many. I fear for thy body’s lovely form, O youth ; for thy mental gifts and the strength of thy divine courage, for thy learning and thy prudent counsel. Such we are told, Drusus, are the children of the blessed immortals.

poems.title: Book IX, 776
poems.author: Diodorus of Sardis
poems.text: The colour and the beauty is worthy of Zeuxis; but Satyreius painted me on a little crystal and gave the pretty miniature to Arsinoe. I am the queen’s own image, and no whit inferior to a large picture.

poems.title: On Paula of Tarentum (Mackail)
poems.author: Diodorus of Sardis
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: Bear witness this my stone house of night that has hidden me, and the wail-circled water of Cocytus, my husband did not, as men say, kill me, looking eagerly to marriage with another; why should Rufinius have an ill name idly? but my predestined Fates lead me away; not surely is Paula of Tarentum the only one who has died before her day.

poems.title: On a Mother, Dead in Childbirth (Mackail)
poems.author: Diodorus of Sardis
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: These woeful letters of Diodorus' wisdom tell that I was engraven for one early dead in child-birth, since she perished in bearing a boy; and I weep to hold Athenaïs the comely daughter of Melo, who left grief to the women of Lesbos and her father Jason; but thou, O Artemis, wert busy with thy beast-slaying hounds.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca 7.700: Ἴστω νυκτὸς ἐμῆς ἣ κέκρυφέ μ᾽ οἰκία ταῦτα
poems.author: Diodorus of Sardis
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology, Greek text (Mackail, 1890)
poems.text:
Ἴστω νυκτὸς ἐμῆς ἣ κέκρυφέ μ᾽ οἰκία ταῦτα
λάϊνα, Κωκυτοῦ τ᾽ ἀμφιγόητον ὕδωρ,
οὔτι μ᾽ ἀνήρ, ὃ λέγουσι, κατέκτανεν ἐς γάμον ἄλλης
παπταίνων· τί μάτην οὔνομα Ῥουφίνιος;
ἀλλά με Κῆρες ἄγουσι μεμορμέναι· οὐ μία δήπου
Παῦλα Ταραντίνη κάτθανεν ὠκύμορος.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca 6.348: Αἴλινον ὠκυμόρῳ με λεχωΐδι τοῦτο κεκόφθαι
poems.author: Diodorus of Sardis
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology, Greek text (Mackail, 1890)
poems.text:
Αἴλινον ὠκυμόρῳ με λεχωΐδι τοῦτο κεκόφθαι
τῆς Διοδωρείου γράμμα λέγει σοφίης,
κοῦρον ἐπεὶ τίκτουσα κατέφθιτο· παῖδα δὲ Μηλοῦς
δεξάμενος θαλερὴν κλαίω Ἀθηναΐδα
Λεσβιάδεσσιν ἄχος καὶ Ἰήσονι πατρὶ λιποῦσαν·
Ἄρτεμι, σοὶ δὲ κυνῶν θηροφόνων ἔμελεν.
